problem:
The entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & k\end{aligned}]$
equals $-\frac{1}{2}$ and $det(A)=-k.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=-k
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{12}^{t}={c}_{21}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{21} & =(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(0+1) \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{12}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{12}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{21} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-k)}\cdot (-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{12}^{′}=-\frac{1}{2}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{k} & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ k & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
